text: Functions used: build_dynamic_networks() build_network() filter_components() step creates one static network (tbl_graph) list temporal networks (list tbl_graph) bipartite links (source_id -> target_id). build_network() single-network wrapper around build_dynamic_networks().

title: Presentation of networkflow
text: build_dynamic_networks() builds one network list time-window networks user provides temporal variable. build_network() wrapper one network build_dynamic_networks(time_variable = NULL). build_dynamic_networks() supports two different filtering strategies: build_dynamic_networks() takes input bipartite relation projects one-mode network. supports two different filtering strategies edge retention projection: structured strategy, defines edge strength using measures derived co-occurrence intensity; statistical strategy, defines null model random co-occurrence keeps edges based statistical significance. short, first approach defines filters observed tie strength, second defines filters statistical significance. structured method generally computationally efficient, statistical method provides rigorous filter connections beyond random chance. example, source_id article target_id reference, structured method keep article pairs strong co-citation bibliographic coupling, statistical method keep article pairs whose co-citation bibliographic coupling significantly stronger expected random model. Parameters common methods: nodes: table one row per source entity defined source_id. directed_edges: table directed edges source_id target_id. source_id, target_id: identifier columns used projection. projection_method: "structured" "statistical". compute_size: TRUE, computes node_size. keep_singleton: FALSE, removes isolated nodes. Structured-parameters (projection_method = "structured") uses cooccurrence/coupling measures biblionetwork package. cooccurrence_method: "coupling_angle", "coupling_strength", "coupling_similarity". edges_threshold: minimum edge strength retained. Statistical-parameters (projection_method = "statistical") uses statistical backbone extraction (backbone package). model: "sdsm", "fdsm", "fixedfill", "fixedrow", "fixedcol". alpha: significance threshold edge retention. backbone_args: additional arguments passed backbone routines. Dynamic-parameters (build_dynamic_networks()): time_variable: temporal column nodes (example publication year). time_window: width window. overlapping_window: rolling windows (TRUE) disjoint windows (FALSE). first case, partition done rolling time window one unit (example, 1990-2009, 1991-2010, etc.). second case, partition done fixed intervals (example, 1990-1999, 2000-2009, etc.). main output functions tbl_graph (list tbl_graph dynamic analyses). projection_method = "structured", output edges weighted selected cooccurrence/coupling measure. projection_method = "statistical", output edges unweighted retained based statistical significance. Examples:
code: library(networkflow)  nodes <- subset(Nodes_stagflation, source_type == "Stagflation")  references <- Ref_stagflation g_static <- build_network(   nodes = nodes,   directed_edges = references,   source_id = "source_id",   target_id = "target_id",   projection_method = "structured",   cooccurrence_method = "coupling_similarity",   edges_threshold = 1,   compute_size = FALSE,   keep_singleton = FALSE ) g_dynamic <- build_dynamic_networks(   nodes = nodes,   directed_edges = references,   source_id = "source_id",   target_id = "target_id",   time_variable = "source_year",   time_window = 20,   projection_method = "structured",   cooccurrence_method = "coupling_similarity",   edges_threshold = 1,   overlapping_window = TRUE,   compute_size = FALSE,   keep_singleton = FALSE ) g_dynamic_stat <- build_dynamic_networks(   nodes = nodes,   directed_edges = references,   source_id = "source_id",   target_id = "target_id",   time_variable = "source_year",   time_window = 20,   projection_method = "statistical",   model = "sdsm",   alpha = 0.05,   overlapping_window = TRUE,   compute_size = FALSE,   keep_singleton = FALSE )

title: Presentation of networkflow
text: Run community detection static dynamic network. function wrapper around tidygraph::group_graph(). also supports igraph implementation Leiden algorithm, default method. Main parameters: clustering_method: clustering algorithm use. weights: edge weight column usage. objective_function, resolution, n_iterations: Leiden controls. seed: reproducibility stochastic algorithms. output tbl_graph (list tbl_graph) new columns: - node column cluster_{method}. - edge columns cluster_{method}_from, cluster_{method}_to, cluster_{method}. - node column size_cluster_{method} cluster shares. Example:
code: g_static <- add_clusters(   graphs = g_static,   clustering_method = "leiden",   objective_function = "modularity",   resolution = 1,   n_iterations = 1000,   seed = 123 ) ## ℹ The leiden method detected 7 clusters. The biggest cluster represents "36.1%" of the network. g_dynamic <- add_clusters(   graphs = g_dynamic,   clustering_method = "leiden",   objective_function = "modularity",   resolution = 1,   n_iterations = 1000,   seed = 123 )

title: Presentation of networkflow
text: add_clusters() runs independently time window, cluster IDs directly comparable across windows. merge_dynamic_clusters() links clusters adjacent windows node overlap high enough, assigns stable intertemporal IDs. Input requirements: list_graph must list least two tbl_graph. list order must chronological (oldest recent window). Main parameters: cluster_id: input cluster column (example cluster_leiden). node_id: stable node identifier across windows. threshold_similarity: matching threshold (0.5, 1]. similarity_type: "complete" "partial". similarity_type controls overlap computed: "complete": overlap share computed nodes compared clusters, including entries exist one window. stricter network size changes time. "partial": overlap share computed nodes present adjacent windows. often preferable many new nodes enter time. Output: new node column dynamic_{cluster_id} (example dynamic_cluster_leiden). dynamic cluster IDs assigned propagation: starts assigning unique IDs clusters first time window, propagates IDs later windows cluster match passes similarity threshold; otherwise, new dynamic ID created. corresponding edge columns dynamic_{cluster_id}_from, dynamic_{cluster_id}_to, dynamic_{cluster_id}.
code: g_dynamic <- merge_dynamic_clusters(   list_graph = g_dynamic,   cluster_id = "cluster_leiden",   node_id = "source_id",   threshold_similarity = 0.51,   similarity_type = "partial" )

title: Presentation of networkflow
text: Cluster IDs informative . name_clusters() helps assign readable labels clusters based content. labels meant definitive cluster names, rather quick way get sense cluster content. function supports three methods: method = "tf-idf": labels clusters distinctive terms extracted text_columns. usually best default thematic interpretation. method = "given_column": selects, within cluster, node highest value order_by, builds label label_columns node. Typically, can use method label clusters title representative article (example cited one). method = "tidygraph_functions": computes centrality measure tidygraph_function, selects central node per cluster, builds label label_columns. Main parameters: method: "tidygraph_functions", "given_column", "tf-idf". name_merged_clusters: TRUE name dynamic clusters across list. Typically, want set TRUE cluster_id dynamic cluster column created merge_dynamic_clusters(). cluster_id: column name. label_name: output label column name ("cluster_label" default). text_columns, nb_terms_label: key arguments TF-IDF naming.
code: g_dynamic <- name_clusters(   graphs = g_dynamic,   method = "tf-idf",   name_merged_clusters = TRUE,   cluster_id = "dynamic_cluster_leiden",   text_columns = "source_title",   nb_terms_label = 3 )

title: Presentation of networkflow
text: Nodes cluster can play different structural roles. add_node_roles() implements Guimera-Amaral classification node roles based two measures: within-module degree (z-score) participation coefficient. Use add_node_roles() clustering classify nodes according structural position modules (within-module degree, participation coefficient, Guimera-Amaral roles). helps distinguish peripheral nodes, connectors, hubs. Main parameters: module_col: cluster/module column used compute roles. weight_col: edge weight column. z_threshold: hub threshold within-module z-score. Main outputs: within_module_degree. within_module_z. participation_coeff. role_ga.
code: g_static <- add_node_roles(   graphs = g_static,   module_col = "cluster_leiden",   weight_col = "weight",   z_threshold = 2.5 )

Main parameters: text_columns: one text fields used extract ngrams. grouping_columns: document units TF-IDF (example cluster IDs). grouping_across_list: helps disambiguate group IDs across windows. n_gram: maximum n ngrams. clean_word_method: "lemmatize", "stemming", "none". ngrams_filter: remove terms rare globally. nb_terms: number top terms returned per group.

title: Launch an Interactive Shiny App to Explore a Network Graph — launch_network_app
text: function launches interactive Shiny application visualizing exploring network graph represented tbl_graph object. supports node cluster interactivity tooltips, dynamic sizing, customizable coloring. Users can inspect clusters interactively explore associated node metadata searchable datatable. app designed cluster/module exploration, cluster_id cluster_information required. graph contain layout (columns x y) function compute coordinates using networkflow::layout_networks() specified layout algorithm.  layout name provided, replace existing layout graph.
